svg.title: Entity-relationship model — three independent stores, one enforced FK graph

g.text: Entity-relationship model — three independent stores, one enforced FK graph
TRUST BOUNDARY — the single Docker `data` volume
mounted read-write into sync-worker AND into the orchestrator that executes LLM-authored SQL (docker-compose.yml:269)
it also holds the Salesforce RSA signing key at /data/sf_jwt_key.pem (syncworker/secrets.py:50)
stdlib sqlite3, one short-lived connection per call — db.py:195-205
ORPHAN DEFECT — the central data-model risk.
`DELETE FROM conversations WHERE id=? AND user_id=?`
(db.py:86, 104, 116, 125). After the delete those rows survive
forever: no cascade, no TTL, no pruning job anywhere in
`orchestrator/app/` — the whole page text, code chunks and
dataset profiles of a "deleted" chat stay readable to anyone
who can guess or replay the conversation id.
`DELETE FROM messages … GROUP BY conversation_id, generation_id`
(db.py:181-186) — a full scan + group-by of `messages` on
so writes fail with "database is locked" after the stdlib
redundant: UNIQUE(conversation_id, ordinal) at db.py:77 already indexes this
WHERE generation_id IS NOT NULL — db.py:187-191 (partial, race fix)
DuckDB has no keys at all.
(storage.py:138-142), which carries no PK, no UNIQUE and
• Nothing prevents duplicate `Id` rows; correctness rests
amounts cannot be compared or aggregated numerically by
the LLM-authored SQL without an explicit CAST.
internal watermark table is handed to the SQL-writing LLM as
if it were a business object.
No dedup and no re-embed guard
the indexer never compares incoming text to what is stored —
no content hash, no `system_modstamp` comparison. Any change
to any field bumps `SystemModstamp`, so every long-text chunk
of that record is re-embedded on the GPU.
different dimension silently appends mismatched vectors.
Why the dashed red boundary matters.
(syncworker/secrets.py:50) all live in ONE Docker volume that is
mounted into the orchestrator (docker-compose.yml:269) — the same
The only thing separating model text from that key is the DuckDB
(sql_guard.py:45-54). There is no filesystem-level isolation and no
no store enforces identity across the boundary
DuckDB/LanceDB carry no key at all.
pinned : INTEGER «DEFAULT 0, added by migrate() db.py:141-144»
archived : INTEGER «DEFAULT 0, added by migrate() db.py:141-144»
content : TEXT «NO INDEX — LIKE full-scans at db.py:963,972,995»
meta : TEXT «JSON blob, json.loads at db.py:352»
: TEXT «PK + FK → conversations(id) ON DELETE CASCADE»
profile : TEXT «JSON — the only data the dataset engine ever sees»
text : TEXT «extracted readable text; source body capped at FETCH_MAX_BYTES=5 MB»
sha : TEXT «"" when git rev-parse fails — core/repo.py:213»
repo_key : TEXT «no FK to repos(repo_key) either»
upsert = DELETE WHERE Id IN (…) + INSERT BY NAME
new columns adopted by ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN
written LAST, after the whole batch loop
vector : fixed_size_list[float32, dim] «no PK, no unique key»
text : string «one chunk of one rag_field»
table or field carrying a data-model
analytics store (DuckDB / LanceDB) — no keys at all
